title: Demand Response Programs — One Program per Service Agreement
content:
## Customer care guidance: holding demand response enrollments across agreements

**Rule.** A customer may hold Demand Response Programs enrollments on several service agreements, one program per service agreement. No other enrollment on the same service agreement is in enrolled or active status. A customer who wants a different program on the same agreement leaves the first one before enrolling, so the same load is never paid twice.

**What is counted, and where it is read**

- The test is made per Electric Service Agreement. Enrollments on the customer's other agreements do not enter it.
- It is read from the company's enrollment records for that service agreement — the status each existing enrollment shows — before the new enrollment is made. It is not taken from the customer's account of what they hold.
- An enrollment counts against the agreement while its status is *enrolled* (accepted, not yet active) or *active*. An enrollment whose status is *unenrolled* or *removed* is not in enrolled or active status.
- There is no limit on the number of agreements of one customer that may each hold an enrollment.

**Condition, judgement, result**

| Other enrollment found on the same service agreement | Status of that enrollment | This rule |
|---|---|---|
| None | — | Satisfied |
| Any program | Enrolled | Not satisfied |
| Any program | Active | Not satisfied |
| Any program | Unenrolled | Satisfied |
| Any program | Removed | Satisfied |

**Illustrations (hypothetical customers)**

1. A business customer holds three service agreements at three sites. Each site's agreement holds one active enrollment in the Commercial Capacity Bidding Program. Each agreement holds one program; the rule is met on each.
2. A household's agreement holds an active Peak Time Rebate enrollment and the customer wants Home Battery Dispatch on the same agreement. The active Peak Time Rebate enrollment is in active status, so the agreement already holds a program; the customer leaves Peak Time Rebate before enrolling in Home Battery Dispatch.
3. A household's agreement shows a Smart Thermostat Rewards enrollment from an earlier year in unenrolled status and nothing else. No other enrollment on the agreement is in enrolled or active status.
